name: Hydroxyurea (MPN cytoreduction, high-risk PV/ET)
disease: Myeloproliferative neoplasms (polycythemia vera and essential thrombocythemia)

biomarkers.note: MPN diagnosis uses driver-mutation testing (JAK2, then CALR and MPL if JAK2-negative). Polycythemia vera is almost always JAK2 V617F positive; essential thrombocythemia is JAK2, CALR or MPL mutated. Hydroxyurea is a first-line cytoreductive agent and is not restricted by driver-mutation type. Per Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloproliferative Neoplasms v2.2026.

treatmentSetting: cytoreduction, first-line for high-risk polycythemia vera (PV-2) and high-risk essential thrombocythemia (ET-2)
lineOfTherapy: first-line cytoreductive therapy for high-risk PV or ET

eligibilityCriteria.requirement: high-risk polycythemia vera or essential thrombocythemia requiring cytoreduction
eligibilityCriteria.locator: v2.2026, PV-2 (treatment for high-risk PV) and ET-2 (treatment for high-risk ET)

drugs.name: Hydroxyurea

provenance.locator: MS-24 hydroxyurea 500 mg/day is a symptomatic-MYELOFIBROSIS figure (subsequently adjusted to individual efficacy and tolerability), NOT a PV/ET starting dose; PV-2/ET-2 list hydroxyurea as first-line cytoreduction with no fixed printed mg dose, titrated to hematologic targets (PV hematocrit below 45%, ET count control; effective therapy benchmarked around 2 g/day per the resistance criteria, MPN approximately line 2090)

drugs.notes: Source: Standard Guidelines (NCCN), Myeloproliferative Neoplasms v2.2026. The treatment algorithms PV-2 and ET-2 list hydroxyurea as first-line cytoreduction but do not print a fixed mg dose because it is titrated to hematologic targets. The 500 mg/day figure appears only in the manuscript (MS-24) for symptomatic MYELOFIBROSIS hyperproliferative manifestations (a cross-indication, not PV/ET), subsequently adjusted to individual efficacy and tolerability. For PV/ET there is NO fixed printed starting dose: hydroxyurea is titrated to hematologic targets (PV hematocrit below 45%; ET platelet and WBC control), with effective therapy benchmarked around 2 g/day per the resistance criteria (MPN approximately line 2090). dosePerUnit is therefore set to VERIFY. Continuous daily oral dosing (days 1 to 28 = continuous); titrate to counts (for PV, target hematocrit below 45%; control platelet and WBC counts and symptoms).

supportiveCare: For polycythemia vera: therapeutic phlebotomy to a target hematocrit below 45% (CYTO-PV data; MPN footnote e), plus low-dose aspirin 81 to 100 mg/day unless contraindicated (PV-1). Hydroxyurea provides cytoreduction on top of these measures for high-risk PV.
For essential thrombocythemia: low-dose aspirin 81 to 100 mg/day for most patients (ET-1); hydroxyurea for cytoreduction in high-risk disease (ET-2).
Aspirin: use with caution in acquired von Willebrand syndrome; higher-dose or twice-daily aspirin only for specific refractory vasomotor symptoms per MPN footnotes.
Discontinue hydroxyurea in anticipation of or during pregnancy; peginterferon is the cytoreductive alternative in pregnancy.

monitoring: CBC with differential to titrate dose to hematologic targets (for PV, hematocrit below 45%)

assessment for hydroxyurea intolerance or resistance (cytopenias at the dose needed for control, leg ulcers or other mucocutaneous toxicity), which would prompt a switch (for example ruxolitinib or peginterferon)

doseModificationRules.text: If cytopenias occur at the dose needed to control counts, or platelets remain above 400 x 10^9/L with WBC below 2.5 x 10^9/L or hemoglobin below 10 g/dL at any hydroxyurea dose, or leg ulcers or other unacceptable mucocutaneous toxicity occur, consider a switch to an alternative (for example ruxolitinib for PV, or peginterferon). Physician decides.

guideline.locator: PV-2 (hydroxyurea first-line cytoreduction for high-risk PV) and ET-2 (high-risk ET); PV-1/ET-1 (aspirin 81 to 100 mg/day; PV phlebotomy to hematocrit below 45%, footnote e, CYTO-PV); MS-24 (hydroxyurea 500 mg/day titrated); driver-mutation testing (JAK2, CALR, MPL) on MPN diagnostic pages

provenanceNote: ONCQIS Standard Protocol draft for hydroxyurea cytoreduction in high-risk polycythemia vera and essential thrombocythemia. The treatment algorithms (PV-2, ET-2) list hydroxyurea as first-line cytoreduction but do not print a fixed mg dose because it is titrated to hematologic targets; the 500 mg/day figure appears only in the manuscript (MS-24) for symptomatic MYELOFIBROSIS hyperproliferative manifestations (a cross-indication, not PV/ET), so the PV/ET starting dose is set to VERIFY; PV/ET hydroxyurea is titrated to hematologic targets (PV hematocrit below 45%, ET platelet and WBC control), with effective therapy benchmarked around 2 g/day per the resistance criteria (MPN approximately line 2090). For PV, therapeutic phlebotomy to a hematocrit below 45% (CYTO-PV, footnote e) and low-dose aspirin 81 to 100 mg/day (PV-1) are companion measures captured in supportiveCare. Biomarker context: JAK2, CALR and MPL driver mutations are diagnostic (PV is almost always JAK2 V617F positive); hydroxyurea itself is not mutation-restricted. histology and treatmentIntent are VERIFY.
